key_insight: Self-Privileged Fine-Tuning (SPFT) uses a frozen initial model with privileged information to emphasize tokens that better predict the ground-truth outcome.
engineering_relevance: SPFT offers a token-weighted alternative to standard supervised fine-tuning for adapting language models to mathematical reasoning and code generation.
method: Analyze how dynamic and static token weighting change the training target distribution.
Use a frozen initial model conditioned on privileged information, such as ground truth, to supply token-level weights.
Prioritize outcome-predictive tokens through a Bayesian interpretation of the privileged prior.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports improvements over standard SFT and other baselines across the main mathematical reasoning and code generation settings, but provides no numerical results.
watch_item: Effectiveness depends on the quality of the frozen privileged prior; static weighting alone does not guarantee useful guidance.
